checklist.item: Can users reach any page in 3 clicks or fewer?
Is the current location always visible (highlighted nav item, breadcrumb, or page title)?
Does the browser/system back button work correctly on every screen?
Are there 7 or fewer top-level navigation items? (If more, use a sidebar instead.)
Is navigation consistent across all pages (same position, same items)?
Does every destructive action provide an undo path?
Are loading states in place for all async operations (skeleton, spinner, or shimmer as appropriate)?
Do modals trap focus and restore it to the trigger element on close?
Can every drag-and-drop interaction also be completed via keyboard?
Are all animations purposeful and under 500ms? Do they respect prefers-reduced-motion?
Are all forms single-column with top-aligned labels?
Is inline validation triggered on blur (not on keystroke, not only on submit)?
Are error messages placed next to the offending field (not in a top-of-page banner)?
Does the submit button show loading/spinner state to prevent double submission?
Are smart defaults pre-filled where the answer can be predicted?
Does the password field have a show/hide toggle? Are password requirements shown before typing?
Is every screen designed for loading, empty (first use), empty (cleared), error, and ideal states?
Do empty states include a clear CTA (not just 'No data found')?
Do error states say what happened, why, and what to do next? Is there a retry button?
Does the screen handle partial state (some sections loaded, some failed) gracefully?
Have edge cases been tested: very long strings, zero values, empty arrays, rapid double-clicks?
Are all touch targets at least 44×44px (ideally 48×48px)?
Are primary actions and navigation placed in the thumb-friendly zone (bottom half of screen)?
Does the layout work correctly on a 320px-wide screen?
Does the keyboard not obscure the focused input field? Is there proper keyboard avoidance?
Are safe areas (notch, home indicator) respected? No interactive elements in the home indicator zone?
Can every action be completed using only a keyboard (Tab, Enter, Space, Escape)?
Do all interactive elements have a visible focus indicator?
Does colour contrast meet WCAG 2.2 AA minimums (4.5:1 normal text, 3:1 large text and UI components)?
Do all images have appropriate alt text (descriptive for informative, empty for decorative)?
Are form inputs properly associated with labels using for/id? Are required fields marked with text, not just colour?
Do error messages use the formula: what happened + why + how to fix? Do they avoid blaming the user?
Do button labels predict the action ('Save changes', not 'OK')? Are destructive action labels explicit?
Is the tone professional, helpful, and human — not too formal, not too casual?
